title: Tulsa filmmaker restores 1967 Patterson-Gimlin Bigfoot film
excerpt: Todd Gatewood's restoration of the Patterson-Gimlin Film will be released Oct. 20, nearly 59 years after the footage was captured.
content:
TULSA, Okla. -

A Tulsa film archivist has completed a new restoration of the Patterson-Gimlin Film, the 1967 footage that has fueled decades of debate over whether it shows a Bigfoot-type creature.

Todd Gatewood, a Tulsa native and photo archivist, said his restoration focuses on preserving the original film and presenting it for contemporary viewers. The restored version is scheduled for release Oct. 20, the 59th anniversary of the day the footage was allegedly captured.

What is the Patterson-Gimlin Film?

The roughly one-minute sequence was filmed by Roger Patterson and Bob Gimlin in Northern California’s Bluff Creek area. It shows an unidentified, human-like figure moving through the landscape.

The footage has remained the subject of scientific, photographic and cultural research, with debate continuing over whether the figure is an actual creature or a person in a costume.

How the Tulsa restoration was done

Gatewood said the project used high-resolution scans of the original 16mm Kodachrome II color film to reconstruct the imagery for modern viewing.

“This isn’t about creating a new version of the film,” Gatewood said. “It’s about historically preserving what was actually recorded to museum-quality standards and giving people the opportunity to examine the footage while respecting the original photographic material.”

How to Watch

The restored footage will be featured in the upcoming documentary “Bigfoot Revealed: The Unseen Patterson-Gimlin Film.”
